Fetch or parse an OHLCV market series

Source: R/ohlcv.R
bourse_ohlcv.Rd

Returns a grounded market_series of open/high/low/close/volume candles for symbol at interval, or a bourse_refusal if it will not stand behind the result. The series's grounding is [unverified] until bourse_catalogue_diff() has diffed the relevant facts against the exchange catalogue – so a consumer on a live order path can gate on is_refusal() and the grounding label rather than trust an unchecked number.

Usage

bourse_ohlcv(
  symbol,
  interval = "1d",
  candles = NULL,
  source = "binance",
  quote_ccy = NULL,
  base_ccy = NULL,
  limit = 500L
)

Arguments

symbol

The instrument symbol, e.g. "BTCUSDT".

interval

The candle interval, e.g. "1d", "1h".

candles

Optional recorded candles (>= 6 columns: open time, open, high, low, close, volume). When supplied, no network call is made.

source

The data source; currently "binance".

quote_ccy, base_ccy

Optional quote/base currency labels for the obs_schema; these are themselves facts and stay [unverified] until grounded.

limit

Maximum candles to fetch live.

Value

A market_series, or a bourse_refusal.

Details

Supply candles (a matrix or data.frame of recorded candles) to parse an offline fixture; omit it to fetch live (requires the suggested httr2 and jsonlite packages).

See also

Other series: bourse_refusal(), is_refusal(), market_series()

Examples

# Offline: parse a small recorded-style fixture (timestamps in ms UTC).
fixture <- cbind(
  open_time = c(1.5e12, 1.5e12 + 86400000),
  open = c(100, 102), high = c(105, 106), low = c(99, 101),
  close = c(102, 104), volume = c(1200, 1500))
bourse_ohlcv("BTCUSDT", interval = "1d", candles = fixture)
#> <market_series> BTCUSDT @ binance [1d]  2 rows  [grounded]
